definitions_and_conventions: The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖_{ψ₂} := inf{s > 0 : E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2}, i.e. the scale associated with Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
The symbol c denotes a positive absolute (universal) constant, not a theorem input and not a specified numerical value; the book's equivalences permit absolute constant factors.
The absolute value is outside the whole sum, so the claim is a two-sided tail bound.

The theorem is formulated in ψ₂ norms. The mean-zero MGF estimate E exp(λX) ≤ exp(Cλ²‖X‖²_{ψ₂}) for all λ ∈ ℝ is an equivalent property used in the proof, not a replacement statement with a separately fixed variance/MGF parameter.
implicit_context: All probabilities and expectations refer to the common underlying probability space.

details: The bound is uniform over N, all families satisfying the three hypotheses, and all t ≥ 0.

contracts.contract_plain_english: There is an unspecified positive universal constant c such that any finite independent family of mean-zero sub-gaussian real random variables satisfies, for every nonnegative threshold, a two-sided Hoeffding tail bound whose scale is the sum of their squared ψ₂ norms. Here ψ₂ is the exponential-square norm defined by the infimum condition E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2. The proof uses the equivalent mean-zero MGF bound only up to absolute constants, multiplies MGFs using independence, converts back to ψ₂ control, and invokes the ψ₂ tail estimate. The printed source leaves the zero-denominator case unstated and must not be read as silently excluding it or as choosing a particular MGF variance proxy.

The weighted result is introduced by applying the preceding general inequality to aᵢXᵢ in place of Xᵢ; the paragraph prints 'apply Theorem 2.6.3', a self-reference in the introduction of Theorem 2.6.3, where the mathematical derivation indicates Theorem 2.6.2.

contracts.contract_plain_english: There is an unspecified positive universal constant c such that, for independent mean-zero sub-gaussian Xᵢ, every deterministic real weight vector a and every nonnegative threshold obey a two-sided tail bound for ∑aᵢXᵢ with denominator K²‖a‖²₂, where K is the maximum ψ₂ norm of the summands. This is obtained by applying the unweighted theorem to aᵢXᵢ, using ψ₂ homogeneity and bounding the exact squared-norm sum by K²‖a‖²₂. The ψ₂ norm remains the exponential-square infimum norm; the MGF bound is only an equivalent proof device up to absolute constants. The source contains a self-referential theorem-number typo in the derivation paragraph and leaves the zero-denominator cases a=0 or K=0 unstated.
